title: Grassia(II)-Geometric Distribution with Time-Varying Covariates
text: dynamic marketing interventions, subscription tracking, clinical regimes covariates evolve time, data must structured person-period (long) format. demonstrate estimation using kb_data_sample, 20-subject random sample included rapid experimentation testing: Note Datasets: kb_data_sample fast-running, 20-subject subset intended quick trials, unit tests, interactive exploration. full empirical analyses, use data(kb_data), contains entire cohort 1,499 subjects (34,506 person-period rows).
code: library(G2Gcov)  # Load the quick-start sample dataset (20 subjects) kb_data_sample<-G2Gcov::kb_data_sample  # Estimate the discrete-time model with dynamic marketing covariates fit_varying <- G2G_varying_MLE(   Surv(week, status) ~ coupon + anyp,   data    = kb_data_sample,   subject = "id" )  # Print parameter estimates, standard errors, and Wald confidence intervals print(fit_varying)  # Plot baseline churn probability distribution across the population (p0) plot_p0(fit_varying)  # Predict individual survival curve S(t) along a specific customer trajectory # (Subject 24 is included in kb_data_sample) customer_path <- kb_data_sample[kb_data_sample$id == 24, c("coupon", "anyp")] G2G_varying_survival(solution = fit_varying, X_mat = customer_path)  # Update for a customer who has survived part of their path: # first half = survived history, second half = planned covariates for the periods ahead n_hist      <- max(1L, floor(nrow(customer_path) / 2)) hist_path   <- customer_path[seq_len(n_hist), ] future_path <- customer_path[-seq_len(n_hist), ]  # Posterior mean of the baseline per-period event probability (p0) given the history G2G_varying_posterior_p0(fit_varying, hist_path)  # Probability of surviving each of the next periods under the planned covariates, # given survival through the history G2G_varying_cond_survival(fit_varying, hist_path, future_path)

title: Grassia(II)-Geometric Distribution with Time-Varying Covariates
text: covariates remain fixed throughout observation (baseline demographics treatment arms), standard survival datasets (like survival::veteran) can modeled directly, including numeric categorical/factor variables: Note posterior functions: time-varying covariates, G2G_varying_posterior_p0() returns baseline probability (absent covariates), can combined planned covariate path. time-invariant covariates later choice covariates, G2G_static_posterior_p() returns subject’s probability, hence name without 0. vignette explains difference.
code: library(G2Gcov) library(survival)  # Load the Veteran dataset veteran<-survival::veteran  # Estimate the static model with numeric (age) and factor (celltype) covariates fit_static <- G2G_static_MLE(   Surv(time, status) ~ age + celltype,   data = veteran )  # Inspect model summary print(fit_static)  # Plot baseline probability distribution (at reference covariate levels) plot_p0(fit_static)  # Predict survival over 10 periods for a specific baseline covariate profile G2G_static_survival(fit_static, data.frame(age = 49, celltype = "squamous"), 10)  # Update for a patient who has survived 30 days (hist = number of survived periods) G2G_static_posterior_p(fit_static, data.frame(age = 49, celltype = "squamous"), hist = 30)  # Probability of surviving each of the next 10 days, given survival through day 30 G2G_static_cond_survival(fit_static, data.frame(age = 49, celltype = "squamous"),                          hist = 30, future = 10)

title: Posterior Mean of the Baseline Per-Period Event Probability Given History — G2G_varying_posterior_p0
text: customer survived t periods covariate path \(z(1), \dots, z(t)\) posterior \(\lambda \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(r, \alpha + C(t))\), \(C(t) = \sum_{j=1}^{t} e^{z(j)\beta'}\). posterior mean \(p_0\) $$1 - \left(\frac{\alpha + C(t)}{\alpha + C(t) + 1}\right)^r.$$ history enters \(C(t)\).

title: G2Gcov 0.1.0
text: Initial CRAN release. G2G_static_MLE(): maximum likelihood estimation G2G models time-invariant covariates. Includes input validation informative error messages missing columns, NA values, non-binary status, degenerate data. Surv() formula read, evaluated, survival package need attached. G2G_varying_MLE(): maximum likelihood estimation G2G models time-varying covariates person-period format. Includes input validation static version plus checks binary status values, positive time periods, presence least one event, events occurring subject’s final period. Rows may supplied order. estimators report r alpha delta-method standard errors natural scale 95% intervals computed log scale. print.G2Gcov(): S3 print method fitted model objects. Displays convergence status, log-likelihood, AIC, formatted parameter table standard errors 95% Wald confidence intervals. plot_p0(): visualize distribution baseline per-period event probability p0 = 1 - exp(-lambda) implied fitted Gamma distribution lambda. plot_survival_insample_g2g(): -sample G2G survivor curve. plot_survival_holdout_g2g(): hold-G2G survivor curve fitted training data. plot_insample_holdout_paper(): paper-style actual-vs-model survival retention plots optional group faceting. model survivor curves chain together mean model retention subjects risk period, mirroring Kaplan-Meier estimator. Includes kb_data, sample person-period dataset used package vignettes, kb_covars_sample, small subset .
